briefing.headline: Data-centre planning has become a national issue in Scotland
briefing.summary: Since the previous snapshot, Scottish Ministers have required councils to notify them about data-centre applications above 50 MW, required environmental assessment for two proposals and recalled the South Gyle appeal. New applications and financing announcements are also moving parts of the pipeline forward, while petitions and local campaigns are increasing scrutiny of cumulative electricity, water, landscape and community impacts.

updates.title: Government promises a responsible-investment framework
updates.summary: The 2026-31 Programme for Government commits ministers to publish a strategic approach during 2026-27, setting expectations for environmental sustainability, resource use, community benefit, and economic and strategic value. It is a future commitment, not a moratorium or guidance already in force.

updates.title: Scottish Ministers introduce notification for data centres above 50 MW
updates.summary: Planning authorities must notify Scottish Ministers within seven days of validating qualifying applications. The direction applies to current as well as new cases and allows ministers to consider whether national-level intervention is needed.

updates.title: Environmental assessment required at Wester Hermiston and Cato
updates.summary: Scottish Ministers reversed the local screening outcomes for the Wester Hermiston and Cato proposals. Cato's live application, and any future Wester Hermiston application, now require an Environmental Impact Assessment before determination.

updates.title: South Gyle appeal recalled for a ministerial decision
updates.summary: The live appeal over Edinburgh Council's refusal of the South Gyle proposal was recalled from the reporter. It remains undecided and is now for Scottish Ministers to determine.

updates.title: Formal Spango Valley application enters the Inverclyde system
updates.summary: The former IBM site proposal moved beyond consultation into a planning-permission-in-principle application for four data-centre buildings and associated works. The application remains pending.

updates.title: DataVita says it has submitted its DV4 application
updates.summary: DataVita announced submission of its Chapelhall DV4 proposal after revising the design. No validated council reference was located by the snapshot date, so the Observatory continues to classify it as pre-application until an official case record is confirmed.

updates.title: Campaign groups coordinate around cumulative national impacts
updates.summary: A joint letter coordinated by APRS brought together campaigners from 14 communities. Separately, Scottish Parliament petition PE2233 asks for a moratorium while cumulative impacts and planning guidance are assessed. Petition and objection totals are time-sensitive campaign-reported figures, not measures of wider public opinion.

caveats: A project count is not a count of schemes likely to be built: records range from operating sites to strategic opportunities and grid-only leads.
Capacity figures describe different things, including IT load, grid import and developer headline capacity. They are kept separate and should not be added without qualification.
Application, objection and petition numbers can change daily. Counts are dated and attributed where the source permits; treat all of them as snapshots rather than measures of wider opinion.

The Scottish Government has said it does not yet maintain a definitive published list of all Scottish data-centre proposals. This Observatory is an independent research dataset, not an official register.

project.summary: In September 2025 AI Pathfinder, a start-up associated with Salamanca Group chairman Martin Bellamy, announced up to £15bn of investment in a 1 GW (potentially 1.5 GW) 'sovereign AI' data centre campus at the i3 enterprise area in Irvine, with operations claimed from 2026. No planning application, PAN, screening or scoping request has ever appeared on the North Ayrshire portal, no grid connection evidence has been published, and no accounts have been filed by the two-month-old holding company behind the claims. In late 2025 the company was paralysed by a shareholder dispute and asset freeze; after a £17.7m management buyout (January 2026) and a High Court judgment (24 July 2026), press reporting states the company effectively ceased operations and the Ayrshire site remains undeveloped.
project.maturity_explanation: M0 concept/marketed only, with the largest claims-vs-evidence gap in this dataset. Evidence for the 1-1.5 GW / £15bn claims consists solely of a company press announcement and council welcome. No planning, grid or land-control evidence has been located. City A.M. reported on 24 July 2026 that the company effectively ceased operations and the Ayrshire site remains undeveloped. The project is therefore classified as paused, while retaining the caveat that the collapse has not been formally confirmed by the company or council.
project.anticipated_operational_date: 2026 (developer claim at announcement; not credible — no planning application ever lodged)

latest_development.headline: High Court rejects co-founder Martin Hughes's challenge to the £17.7m management buyout; City A.M. reports AI Pathfinder effectively ceased operations and the Ayrshire site remains undeveloped

unknowns: Whether AI Pathfinder (or any successor to the management buyout) retains any interest in the i3 Irvine site, or whether the project is formally dead
Whether any land option, missive or heads of terms over i3 land was ever agreed with North Ayrshire Council or other landowners — no evidence found
Whether any grid connection application was made to SPEN/NESO for the claimed 1,000 MW — no public record found
The exact parcel(s) within/around the i3 area intended for the campus (the ~196 acres reported by City A.M. exceeds obviously available i3 plots)
Source of the £15bn figure and any committed (rather than aspirational) funding beyond the ~£100m seed round
Whether North Ayrshire Council has issued any statement since the company's reported collapse (its original welcome page now returns 404)

site_area_m2.notes: City A.M. describes a ~196-acre (~79 ha) Ayrshire site; no plan, address or title evidence published, and no red-line boundary exists. Figure recorded as reported, not verified.

site.current_land_use: i3 is North Ayrshire's Enterprise Area for life sciences and advanced manufacturing (Riverside Way / Annickbank area), a mix of occupied industrial premises and serviced development plots
site.land_notes: Announcement located the project only in 'the i3 area of Irvine'. No specific plot, address, land option or acquisition has been identified; coordinates are an approximate centroid of the i3 area and should not be treated as a site location. No evidence of land control was found.

capacity_claims.preferred_rationale: The only capacity figures that exist are the developer's own announcement numbers; no planning or grid documentation corroborates any of them.
capacity_claims.notes: Announced as a '1GW site' with initial deployment of up to 6,400 GPUs (a GPU count consistent with only tens of MW of IT load, far below 1 GW — internal inconsistency in the claim). Whether 1 GW refers to IT load or grid import was never specified.
'Future potential to expand to 1.5GW', which would make it 'one of the largest AI infrastructure hubs in Europe'. No supporting planning, land or grid evidence.

capacity_claims.claimant: Stop Climate Chaos Scotland (characterising the developer claim)
capacity_claims.notes: Campaigners cite the site as requiring 1,000 MW, equivalent to ~25% of Scotland's peak electricity demand. This restates the developer figure; no connection application has been identified.

economic_claims.methodology: None published
economic_claims.notes: 'Up to £15bn' announced September 2025. Only ~£100m of seed funding was ever reported as raised across the whole company before its January 2026 buyout, a ~150x gap between claim and evidenced funding.

economic_claims.methodology: None published
economic_claims.notes: £385m initial deployment (up to 6,400 GPUs) claimed at announcement; no evidence any spend occurred.
'Substantial employment' across construction, operations and supply chain claimed; no numbers, categories or methodology ever published.

planning_cases.description: Negative finding: no planning trail exists. Searches of the North Ayrshire Council e-planning portal on 2026-07-30 for 'data centre' and 'i3 Irvine' found no application, Proposal of Application Notice, EIA screening request or scoping request relating to AI Pathfinder or any data centre at the i3 area. The only data-centre record in North Ayrshire is 26/00138/EIA (Hunterston Estate — an unrelated project). A 1-1.5 GW campus would be a 'major'/'national' development requiring a PAN and at minimum 12 weeks of pre-application consultation before any application, making the announced 2026 operations date impossible even at the time it was made.

organisations.name: AI Pathfinder Inc Limited
organisations.ownership_summary: Holding-company SIC code (64209); incorporated 23 May 2025, four months before the £15bn announcement, with no accounts filed (first due Feb 2027). Press reporting describes an Isle of Man holding company formed mid-2025 as the founding shareholder, a ~£100m seed round at a £500m valuation in November 2025, an asset freeze during shareholder litigation, and a £17.7m management buyout in January 2026 upheld by the High Court on 24 July 2026.
organisations.notes: A sibling entity, AI PATHFINDER HOLDINGS LIMITED (16926656), was incorporated 22 Dec 2025 at the same registered office (58 Grosvenor Street, London W1K 3JB) — timing consistent with the reported management buyout restructuring. City A.M. reports the operating business effectively ceased after the buyout.

organisations.name: Salamanca Group

Press described AI Pathfinder as a Salamanca subsidiary/affiliate; the exact corporate relationship was never documented publicly and Companies House shows AI Pathfinder Inc Limited as a standalone holding company.

project.canonical_name: Blackdog Data Centre and AI Campus
project.summary: Proposed 'multi-gigawatt' hyperscale AI data centre campus on around 200 acres at Blackdog, five miles north of Aberdeen, including a former MoD firing range, announced in April 2026 by Ashfield Land and TechRE with an initial 600 MW phase claimed. No data-centre planning application has been lodged: the 'planning consent already secured' claim rests on a 2016 planning permission in principle (APP/2016/0766) for a mixed-use town centre/business scheme, with which the developers say the data centre plans would align. Powering the site from offshore wind (ScotWind/INTOG, Cerulean Winds' Aspen) via private wire is described as under discussion, not contracted.
project.maturity_explanation: Land assembled by the developers and a prior planning permission in principle (APP/2016/0766, mixed use, not a data centre) exists on the site, but no data-centre application, EIA screening/scoping or PAN has been located on the Aberdeenshire portal or in reporting; APRS and press state detailed planning is yet to be submitted. Announcement stage with claimed 'planning foundations' — early development, not M2/M3 for the data centre itself.
project.anticipated_construction_start: 2026 (developer hope, 'first ground broken', subject to final commercial agreements)

phases.description: Initial 600 MW of 'renewable and grid connected power'; developers state planning consent 'already secured' for the first phase, apparently relying on the 2016 mixed-use PPiP rather than any data-centre-specific permission.
Aspiration to scale to a multi-gigawatt data centre and AI campus; no capacity figure, application or grid evidence located for this ambition.

latest_development.headline: Developers Ashfield Land and TechRE announce 600 MW initial / multi-gigawatt data centre and AI campus at Blackdog, citing existing first-phase consent and hoped 2026 start

unknowns: Formal decision date, conditions and any section 75 obligations of PPiP APP/2016/0766 (Aberdeenshire Idox portal unreachable during research; committee approval 27 Apr 2017, ministerial clearance 22 Aug 2017, issue of decision notice not confirmed)

Which corporate entity is the applicant/SPV for the data centre (no Blackdog data centre SPV located at Companies House; TechRE has multiple Edinburgh-registered entities)
Any grid connection application/offer with SSEN Transmission or NESO for 600 MW import — no evidence found beyond developer statements
Whether any contractual arrangement exists with Cerulean Winds (Aspen) or any ScotWind/INTOG project — reported only as 'discussions' and 'exploring'
Operator or anchor tenant — none named
Exact site boundary of the 200-acre data centre landholding versus the earlier 71-acre mixed-use consent area
Whether remediation of the contaminated former landfill in the dunes south of the site affects the developable area

site.site_name: Land at Blackdog (including former MoD rifle range), east of the A90 at the AWPR junction

site_area_m2.claimant: Ashfield Land / TechRE press release (approx. 200 acres)
site_area_m2.notes: 200 acres converted to m2; described as 'around 200 acres'. The earlier consented mixed-use development was described by Energetica as 71 acres, so the data centre landholding is substantially larger than the 2016 PPiP town-centre area.

site.current_land_use: Largely undeveloped coastal land including former MoD firing range; adjacent Blackdog village, industrial estate and ongoing housing development (Kirkwood/Persimmon)
site.previous_land_use: Ministry of Defence rifle/firing ranges; part of wider Blackdog Masterplan area allocated in 2012 Aberdeenshire LDP; former oil-and-gas waste landfill in dunes immediately south of the site (designated contaminated land 2004, remediation project approved 2019)
site.land_notes: Site sits on the Energetica corridor at the junction of the A90 and the Aberdeen Western Peripheral Route. APRS notes the site is on the edge of the dune system. Historic contamination is in the dunes directly south of the development land, not confirmed within the red line. Coordinates are an approximate centroid of the land east of the A90 around the former rifle range; no red-line boundary for the data centre has been published, so no boundary polygon is provided. Official red-line area (Spatial Hub, planning application boundary): 39.6 ha; previously recorded 80.9 ha (developer-stated landholding); difference -51%. EXPECTED: the official red line belongs to the 2016 mixed-use PPiP (APP/2016/0766), a different and smaller scheme than the ~200-acre (80.9 ha) data-centre landholding. Consistent with the existing finding that the claimed 'consent' is not a data-centre consent.

capacity_claims.preferred_rationale: Only figure given for the initial phase; consistently reported across outlets, but appears in no planning or grid document located.
capacity_claims.notes: Described as 'an initial 600 megawatts of both renewable and grid connected power'. No planning application or grid connection evidence for 600 MW was located.
'Multi-gigawatt' campus ambition — no specific figure. Recorded with minimum 1,000 MW purely as the literal floor of 'multi-gigawatt'; aspirational and unsupported by any application or grid record.

Claim of 'access to three gigawatts of renewably generated wind energy' — refers to potential offshore wind (ScotWind/INTOG, Cerulean Winds Aspen) that might be linked by private wire, not on-site generation or a contracted supply. Recorded as a claim of available renewable supply, not capacity of the facility.

economic_claims.methodology: Not stated; 'around 1,000 construction jobs' at full scale — whether peak headcount, average or job-years is unstated
economic_claims.notes: Category assigned as peak/around figure for construction; press release does not distinguish direct vs indirect or FTE vs headcount. Conditional on full-scale delivery.

economic_claims.methodology: Not stated; 'around 100 highly skilled permanent roles'
economic_claims.notes: The only permanent direct employment figure — two orders of magnitude below the combined construction/indirect headlines. FTE status unstated; appears to relate to the campus at scale.

economic_claims.geographic_scope: Region ('across engineering, digital services and R&D')
economic_claims.methodology: Not stated; 'up to 2,000 indirect jobs' — no multiplier methodology or consultant named
economic_claims.notes: 'Up to' figure, contingent on full-scale delivery; no distinction between indirect and induced.

economic_claims.period: per gigawatt of data centre capacity
economic_claims.methodology: Rule of thumb: 'a single gigawatt of data centre capacity requiring over £10 billion pounds to develop'; 'billions of pounds in private investment' at full scale

economic_claims.period: long term, once mixed-use development complete
economic_claims.claimant: Ashfield Land / Kirkwood Homes (2016, for the consented mixed-use scheme, NOT the data centre)
economic_claims.methodology: Developer statement for the 2016 £150m mixed-use application: 1,200 construction jobs and 1,500 net additional full-time jobs long term, £586m salaries over 25 years, £1.56bn GVA
economic_claims.notes: Recorded for context of the consent the data centre relies on. These figures relate to the town centre/housing scheme, not the data centre, and are superseded by the 2026 data centre claims for this site's future.

planning_cases.description: Mixed Use Development Comprising Town Centre Including Regional Food Hall, Retail, Leisure and Class 3 Uses; Business and Industrial Uses (Classes 4, 5 and 6); Alterations to Access from A90 Roundabout, Local Access, Landscaping, Car Parking, Cycle and Pedestrian Facilities and Low Carbon Infrastructure — Land to West and South West of Rifle Range, Blackdog, Aberdeen. This is the pre-existing consent the data centre developers cite: they state planning consent is 'already secured' for the first phase and that they 'believe plans for the multi-billion pound data centre would align with these conditions'. It is not a data centre permission.
planning_cases.decision_notes: Unanimous approval by Formartine Area Committee (March 2017) and full council (27 April 2017) per developer/Energetica accounts. The application was notified to Scottish Ministers (case NA-ABS-045) and cleared back to Aberdeenshire Council for its own determination on 22 August 2017; the formal decision notice, its date, conditions and any section 75 agreement could not be inspected because the Aberdeenshire Idox portal was unreachable during research. Submission date approximate ('March 2016' per Energetica; developer press release 18 April 2016).
planning_cases.conditions_summary: Not obtained — portal unreachable. Developers assert the data centre would 'align with these conditions' (their words), which is the key untested claim.

community.summary: Announcement-stage project; no statutory consultation for a data-centre application has occurred. The developers commissioned a poll (True North Advisors / Diffley Partnership) reporting 62% of 1,303 people across Aberdeen and Aberdeenshire in favour of a 'green data centre, industrial and energy park' at Blackdog. Organised local scrutiny is now represented by AI Data Centres Awareness Group – Blackdog, Balmedie and surrounding area, a signatory to the August 2026 community-campaign coalition letter. APRS has added Blackdog to its data-centres campaign map and questions whether offshore wind should power data centres. Regional economic development bodies ONE and ETZ Ltd publicly support the project.

claimed_local_benefits.benefit: Around 1,000 construction jobs, ~100 permanent high-skilled roles, up to 2,000 indirect jobs, billions of pounds of private investment and a 'just transition' route for oil and gas workers

stakeholder_positions.position: Critical scrutiny: highlights that only a 2016 mixed-use PPiP exists, that detailed planning is yet to be submitted, that the site adjoins a dune system and a toxic oil-and-gas waste dump, and questions whether Scotland's offshore wind should be used for data centres.
Supportive: CEO Jennifer Craw says the north east's access to offshore wind gives it a competitive edge for hyperscale AI investment.
Supportive of the project as part of regional energy transition and digital economy ambitions.

Supportive as prospective power supplier: 'clean power enabling digital growth, and digital demand accelerating renewable deployment' (Laura Jarvie), while noting Aspen will first supply the grid and decarbonise oil and gas platforms.

The coalition letter establishes the local awareness group's participation but does not provide a project-specific objection count. Belhelvie Community Council covers the Blackdog area and has commented on other local applications; its position on the data centre was not located.

requested_import_capacity_mw.notes: The 600 MW initial figure is described as 'both renewable and grid connected power'; no evidence located that a 600 MW connection application or offer exists with SSEN Transmission/NESO.

grid.evidence_basis: Developer press release and journalism only. The offshore-wind narrative is explicitly exploratory: developers are 'exploring the potential for private-wire connections' to ScotWind/INTOG projects, and 'discussions are taking place' with Cerulean Winds over the feasibility of a link from the Aspen floating wind farm. Cerulean's own quote frames Aspen as supplying the grid first, with private-wire to industrial users 'as the project scales up'. TechRE claims 'access to three gigawatts of renewably generated wind energy, significant grid connections and the ability to bring international subsea cables' — none evidenced in any regulatory, NESO or planning document found. On present evidence the offshore wind link is rhetorical/prospective, not contractual.
grid.notes: No SSEN substation, connection voltage, queue position or Gate 2 status identified for this project. Region context: proximity to landfall of ScotWind/INTOG projects north of Aberdeen is the basis of the developers' power narrative.

project.summary: Brightsolid's Aberdeen facility is a purpose-built Tier III-certified colocation data centre in the Mastrick/Whitemyres area of Aberdeen, opened in 2017 and notable as the main commercial colocation site serving the north-east and the oil and gas sector. Public material describes a ~1 MW IT load initially, a ~2 MW two-hall design with up to 400 high-density racks (25 kW/rack) and Ecofris cooling at ~1.25 PUE. Brightsolid is part of Dundee-based DC Thomson; it also operates a Dundee data centre.
project.maturity_explanation: Opened 2017 per Data Center Dynamics and operator technical specification; still marketed as operating in directories as of July 2026.
unknowns: Current built-out capacity vs the 2 MW two-hall design
Formal confirmation of Uptime Institute Tier III certification scope (design vs constructed facility)
Whether announced timelines (2015 announcement, 2017 opening) reflect phased delivery

Both are preserved: the two postcode centroids are only about 120 m apart and Whitemyres Avenue runs off Lang Stracht within the same DC Thomson / Aberdeen Journals complex, so they are almost certainly two descriptions of the same site rather than two sites. Coordinates derive from the Royal Mail postcode unit centroid returned by the postcodes.io API for the postcode recorded above. No building number is published, so the point is a site centroid rather than a door-level fix. Earlier snapshots deliberately coarsened this site; that suppression was lifted on 2026-07-30 because all of it is already public.

project.summary: Proposed ~600 MW hyperscale AI/cloud data centre campus of around £5bn on farmland north-west of Auchtertool village, Fife, promoted by ILI Group through SPV ILI Cato Limited. A planning permission in principle application (26/01243/PPP) was validated by Fife Council on 21 May 2026 for a campus of six to seven data hall buildings up to 35 m high (~280,000 m2 of buildings), gatehouses, substations and infrastructure. Fife Council's 1 April 2026 screening opinion said EIA was not required, but Scottish Ministers subsequently considered the proposal through DPEA case EIA-250-002 and directed on 17 August 2026 that an EIA is required. The first of ILI's three planned 'Stoics' data centres (with Rufus, East Ayrshire, and Aurelius, North Lanarkshire). The application drew over 1,200 published objections and reportedly 14,000-16,000 total representations, plus a SEPA holding objection on flooding.
project.maturity_explanation: Formal planning permission in principle application 26/01243/PPP was validated by Fife Council on 21 May 2026 and remains undetermined. It was preceded by PAN 25/00552/PAN and council EIA screening 25/03079/SCR. Scottish Ministers' later screening direction EIA-250-002, issued 17 August 2026, requires an Environmental Impact Assessment for the proposal.

community.summary: Opposition to the Cato application is among the largest recorded for a Scottish data centre proposal: 1,200+ objections were published on Fife Council's portal by the 24 July 2026 deadline, and the council reported 14,000-16,000 total representations. The objection/support split for that larger total is unknown, so it is not treated as an objection count. Auchtertool Community Council (the village has ~215 houses / ~250 residents) formally objected, having initially acted as a neutral facilitator; a local campaign group 'Say No to Cato' and national group APRS are active; petitions gathered 8,000+ signatures against the development and 2,500+ for a Scottish moratorium on hyperscale data centres. SEPA lodged a holding objection on flooding. Fife Council's decision that no EIA was required drew particular criticism; Scottish Ministers subsequently directed on 17 August 2026 that an EIA is required. ILI has defended the scheme and met residents (including a well-attended June 2026 village hall meeting and further meetings announced in July 2026).

project.canonical_name: Cockenzie data centre (former power station coal store)
project.summary: Council-led proposal for a hyperscale data centre on approximately 70 acres of the former coal store at the demolished Cockenzie power station, East Lothian. East Lothian Council owns the 92 ha site (bought from ScottishPower in 2018) and, following a competitive tender agreed via a private report to Council in February 2025 and announced on 22 October 2025, is negotiating a joint venture with preferred bidder Sustainable Development Capital LLP (SDCL). The council would lease the land to the JV with no capital contribution; financial return and community-benefits framework are still being negotiated. Pre-site due diligence is under way; no planning application has been submitted.
project.maturity_explanation: Concept stage: preferred bidder selected and joint-venture negotiations under way, but no PAN, screening/scoping or planning application has been located; council states the statutory public consultation stage is still ahead, with legal agreements expected to take up to a year from October 2025.

Capital investment value and jobs figures

site.land_notes: Described by APRS and the applicant's EIA as brownfield (ex-opencast, historic mining disturbance), but the land includes Drumshangie Moss peatland with organic soils/peat recorded on site, so it is recorded here as mixed. The site encompasses the location of the 1918 Stanrigg pit disaster: 19 miners died when peat moss inrushed the Arbuckle Pit; 11 bodies were never recovered and remain entombed, with a memorial c.100 m from the accident site. NLC LDP 2022 allocated parts of the landholding as NLC00520 (Data Centre, Greengairs Road, 65.30 ha) and NLC00519 (Energy Plant, 29.52 ha); APRS states the most recent development plan position switched the site toward mixed use. Coordinates are APRS's stated point for the proposal, not a verified red-line centroid. Official red-line area (Spatial Hub, planning application boundary): 235.8 ha; previously recorded 117.2 ha (reported); difference +101%. The official red line for PAN 24/01025/PAN encloses ~235.8 ha against the ~117.2 ha in the sale particulars. Active PSC is Felstead Ford Limited (50-75%), whose sole PSC is Adrian Ashley Hill (b. June 1978) — the ultimate beneficial owner on the Companies House record. Press descriptions of Apatura as 'founded in 2014' and privately owned conflict with the 2022 incorporation date.
organisations.notes: Named by APRS as the developer for the 2026 Drumshangie PAN. Apatura describes a 10.6GW grid-secured portfolio incl. 1.8GW targeting data centres and is progressing several central-belt data centre sites (Ravenscraig 550MW, Larbert/Falkirk, a relocated c.300MW campus, and a 200MW East Ayrshire site) plus multiple BESS projects. Its named applicant entity for Drumshangie is unconfirmed.

organisations.name: Apatura DC Ltd
organisations.ownership_summary: Data-centre holding company incorporated 25 October 2024; PSCs are Apatura Ltd (75%+) and Adrian Ashley Hill (right to appoint/remove directors). Ten numbered SPVs (Apatura DC Project 1-10 Ltd) were incorporated 28 October 2024 at the same address — Apatura's pattern is one numbered SPV per data centre site (e.g. Apatura DC Project 3 Ltd was reported as applicant for its Coldstream/relocated campus).
organisations.notes: It is not yet known which (if any) Apatura DC Project SPV fronts Drumshangie.

organisations.name: Felstead Ford Limited
organisations.ownership_summary: Majority shareholder (50-75%) of Apatura Ltd; sole PSC is Adrian Ashley Hill (75%+ shares and voting rights), identity verified December 2025.

organisations.name: Albert Bartlett Ltd (Albert Bartlett group)
organisations.ownership_summary: The Airdrie-headquartered Albert Bartlett potato group (Albert Bartlett & Sons (Airdrie) Limited SC037896, Albert Bartlett Holdings Limited SC531407, Albert Bartlett Properties Limited SC646257 — all at 251 Stirling Road, Airdrie, adjoining the site). The July 2024 East Airdrie EIA names 'Albert Bartlett Ltd' as applicant and states it is 'in full ownership of the Site'. Trade press describes the 2024 data centre filings as by 'an affiliate of UK potato-supplier Albert Bartlett'.
organisations.notes: Exact registered entity holding the Drumshangie land and lodging PAN 24/01025/PAN unconfirmed. The 117 ha campus site was simultaneously marketed for sale via Shepherd, suggesting the landowner sought a developer/purchaser — consistent with Apatura's subsequent 2026 PAN.

organisations.name: Shepherd Chartered Surveyors
organisations.notes: Selling agent marketing the 117.21 ha Digital/Data Centre & Manufacturing Campus, East Airdrie (contact Steven Barnett, Glasgow office); source of the site area, floorspace and grid-application figures.

organisations.name: Action to Protect Rural Scotland (APRS)
organisations.notes: Scottish charity (SC016139) tracking data centre proposals; maintains the Drumshangie page highlighting the Stanrigg disaster site and development-plan history.

community.summary: Formal community reaction is at an early stage (pre-application). The principal sensitivity flagged publicly is that the site encompasses the location of the 1918 Stanrigg pit disaster, where 19 miners died and 11 remain entombed under the moss, with a memorial adjacent; APRS also highlights the peatland (Drumshangie Moss) and the development-plan history of the site. No community council or resident-group representations were located as of 30 July 2026 — the statutory consultation stage will follow any Planning Permission in Principle application.

principal_concerns.concern: The proposal area encompasses the Stanrigg pit disaster site and its memorial; 11 of the 19 victims of the 1918 inrush were never recovered and remain entombed at the site, making ground disturbance highly sensitive.
principal_concerns.raised_by: APRS (highlighted on its Drumshangie tracking page)

principal_concerns.concern: Loss/disturbance of Drumshangie Moss peatland: organic soils/peat and two local nature conservation designations (Drumshangie Moss North SINC; Drumshangie Moss: Dykehead (South) SINC) are recorded on the wider landholding.
principal_concerns.raised_by: APRS; designations documented in the applicant's own July 2024 East Airdrie EIA

principal_concerns.concern: Development-plan status: the land was allocated for a data centre (NLC00520) and energy plant (NLC00519) in the NLC LDP 2022, but APRS states the most recent development-plan position moved the site toward mixed use, raising questions over policy support for a 500MW campus.

stakeholder_positions.position: Tracking the proposal on its national data centre map; flags the Stanrigg disaster site, the moss and the LDP history. Has not published a formal objection at pre-application stage.

community.notes: The Stanrigg Memorial was assessed only as a visual receptor (Viewpoint 7, 'slight' effects) in the separate Albert Bartlett East Airdrie mixed-use EIA of July 2024; how the data centre proposal treats the memorial and the unrecovered remains has not yet been published.

requested_import_capacity_mw.claimant: Shepherd Chartered Surveyors (selling agent, on behalf of landowner)
requested_import_capacity_mw.notes: Sale particulars state a grid connection application was submitted on 21 October 2024 for 500MW planned demand capacity.

grid.evidence_basis: Selling agent's sale particulars only; no network operator, NESO queue entry, connection offer, voltage or substation identified. The site sits in the SP Energy Networks licence area, but the counterparty to the application was not disclosed.
grid.notes: APRS repeats the 500MW grid-application figure. Whether Apatura's 2026 proposal relies on this same application, and whether it survived the 2025-26 connections-queue reform (Gate 1/Gate 2), is unknown.

aliases.alias: Green Energy Data Centre and Community Renewable Heat Hub, Land South of the A1 at West Barns Mains

project.summary: Proposed 'green energy data centre and community renewable heat hub' by Thistle Sands Data Ltd on approximately 60.2 ha of prime (Class 2 and 3.1) agricultural land south of the A1 at West Barns Mains, on the southern edge of Dunbar, East Lothian. The proposal is pre-application: an EIA screening request (25/00008/SCR) led East Lothian Council to determine that EIA is required, and the Council issued a formal EIA scoping opinion on 30 March 2026. The proposed development includes data centre buildings, substations, district heating infrastructure, access roads, parking, landscaping and drainage. No electrical capacity (MW) has been disclosed. An organised local opposition group exists and campaign groups describe the scheme as hyperscale given the site area.
project.maturity_explanation: Early development / pre-application: EIA screening under reference 25/00008/SCR concluded EIA is required (per APRS summary of the council decision), and East Lothian Council issued an EIA scoping opinion on 30 March 2026 in response to a scoping request received 30 January 2026. No planning application, and no Proposal of Application Notice, has been located.

latest_development.headline: East Lothian Council issues EIA scoping opinion for the West Barns Mains data centre and community renewable heat hub (25/00008/SCR)

unknowns: No electrical capacity (MW) figure has been disclosed by the developer or any other party; APRS explicitly states 'Capacity not known'.

The applicant's EIA Screening Report and Scoping Report have not been located online (the East Lothian planning portal was unreachable during research); details of the two reported SPEN grid connection offers are unknown.
No economic claims (jobs, investment, GVA) by the developer or any party have been located.
Whether a Proposal of Application Notice (PAN) has been lodged is unknown.
Corporate backers/funders of Thistle Sands Data Ltd beyond its two individual shareholders (Kenneth Ross and Steve Ruggi) are unknown; no accounts filed yet (incorporated May 2025).
A reported site figure of up to 62.5 ha could not be corroborated; all located sources state approximately 60.2 ha.
Water demand, cooling method, backup generation fuel and energy use are all undisclosed.
Landowner and any land option arrangements are unknown.

site.address: Land South Of The A1 At West Barns Mains, Dunbar, East Lothian

site_area_m2.claimant: East Lothian Council scoping opinion (approximately 60.2 hectares)

max_building_height_m.claimant: Applicant ZTV modelling assumption reported in council scoping opinion
max_building_height_m.notes: ZTV figures were based on a building height of approximately 12 m excluding roof-mounted plant, described as 'worst-case'; the council's Landscape Officer noted this excludes plant and platform levels, and the Bell briefing states height parameters are not yet fixed. Not a committed design parameter.

site.agricultural_land_class: Class 2 and 3.1 (prime agricultural land, per East Lothian Council scoping opinion); campaign material describes it as Grade 2
site.current_land_use: Arable farmland (three fields)

nearest_home_distance_m.claimant: APRS (homes on Muirfield Road and Home Avenue, Dunbar)
nearest_home_distance_m.notes: Campaign-stated distance, consistent with the council scoping opinion identifying noise-sensitive receptors at Easter Broomhouse Cottages (immediate south), Bowerhouse (west) and Wester Broomhouse Farm (southeast) and the Bell briefing's description of the site as directly adjacent to existing dwellings.

protected_designations: Site lies within the boundaries of the Battle of Dunbar I (BTL31) and Battle of Dunbar II (BTL7) inventory historic battlefields (per HES comments in scoping opinion)
Firth of Forth SPA/Ramsar approximately 1.5 km away (per council Biodiversity Officer comments); Outer Firth of Forth SPA and St Andrews Bay Complex SPA qualifying species recorded within 2 km

Nearby scheduled monuments: Eweford Cottages pit alignment and settlements (SM5835), Eweford Cottages enclosure (SM5834), Bowerhouse enclosure (SM5833), Easter Broomhouse standing stone (SM739), Doon Hill forts (SM5764)
Bower House Dovecot (Category A listed, LB14757) on western periphery of the site
site.land_notes: The council scoping opinion states the site is within Class 2 and 3.1 prime agricultural land; SEPA notes Class 0 mineral soils (no peat/carbon-rich soils). Spott Burn and the water table were flagged by the council Biodiversity Officer as requiring assessment given expected water demand. Habitats Regulations Appraisal is required.

capacity_claims.claimant: None — no MW figure published by developer or any other party
capacity_claims.notes: APRS states 'We do not know what the Capacity of this site would be but, given the size of the site it will be a hyperscale data centre'. The Bell briefing notes the applicant's EIA Screening Report 'provides no details of the scale of power demand from the data centre' despite mentioning two SPEN grid connection offers. No capacity figure appears in any located source.

planning_cases.description: EIA screening for a proposed green energy data centre and community renewable heat hub on land south of the A1 at West Barns Mains, Dunbar (~60.2 ha). The applicant's Screening Report (dated around November 2025 per the Bell critique) argued no significant environmental effects were likely; East Lothian Council determined that an Environmental Impact Assessment is required (as reported by APRS; the council's screening opinion document itself has not been located because the planning portal was unreachable).

events.title: Simon Bell critique of the EIA Screening Report sent to East Lothian Council
events.description: Briefing by Professor Simon Bell arguing that EIA should be required, submitted to inform the EIA screening process.

planning_cases.description: EIA scoping under the same council reference (council internal ref EIA/SCOPING/26/02). Scoping request from Young Planning & Energy Consenting received 30 January 2026 with a Scoping Report dated 28 January 2026. Scoping opinion issued 30 March 2026: population/human health, soil, water, air quality and climatic factors formally scoped out of EIA in the opinion's table, although the Climate Change Officer advised lifecycle GHG, energy demand, water usage and waste heat should be scoped in; biodiversity, flooding, cultural heritage and landscape scoped in; Habitats Regulations Appraisal required; consultees included Scottish Water, NatureScot, Historic Environment Scotland and SEPA. The Biodiversity Officer was unable to agree with the Scoping Report as presented and the Landscape Officer required a 6 km study area and revised ZTVs.
planning_cases.decision_notes: Scoping opinion addressed to Grant Young, Young Planning & Energy Consenting.

organisations.name: Thistle Sands Data Limited

Two directors: Kenneth Ross (appointed on incorporation, born September 1948, resident Scotland) and Steve Ruggi (appointed 31 October 2025, born January 1962, resident England). Persons with significant control are the same two individuals, each with 25-50% of shares and voting rights and the right to appoint or remove directors. No corporate parent or institutional investor is registered; no accounts filed yet.

organisations.notes: Consulted at scoping; cited no objections; requires Pre-Development Enquiry before any technical application and will not accept surface water into the combined sewer.

organisations.name: Opposition to the West Barns Mains Data Centre
organisations.notes: Local opposition Facebook group set up in response to the proposals; reported at 705 members by the East Lothian Courier. Linked from APRS and Sustaining Dunbar pages.

organisations.notes: National charity campaigning against data centre development on rural land; maintains a dedicated Dunbar (West Barns Mains) page and hosts key documents.

organisations.name: Sustaining Dunbar
organisations.notes: Local sustainability charity urging residents to oppose the development and supporting calls for a Scottish Government moratorium on hyperscale AI data centre applications.

community.summary: Organised local opposition exists at pre-application stage. A dedicated Facebook group, Opposition to the West Barns Mains Data Centre (reported 705 members), was set up in response to the proposals, while Dunbar Against Massive Datacentres is named in the national community-campaign coalition. Local charity Sustaining Dunbar urges residents to oppose the scheme, and campaigners are coordinating with APRS to seek a Scottish Government moratorium on hyperscale AI data-centre decisions. APRS's coalition letter recorded 2,465 signatures on the Dunbar petition as at 22 August; the petition displayed 3,161 when checked on 3 September. Statutory and internal-consultee concerns raised at scoping include ecology, water abstraction, heritage, landscape and prime agricultural land. No community benefits have been claimed by the developer in any located source.

principal_concerns.raised_by: APRS; Sustaining Dunbar; Simon Bell briefing

The Screening Report itself has not been located, and no NESO/TEC register entry has been matched to this project. The proposed development includes new on-site substation(s) per the council scoping opinion. The site is roughly 6 km west of Torness power station and its 400 kV connection point, but no source links the project to Torness infrastructure — treat any such link as unverified.
grid.notes: Connection status 'offer' is based solely on the reported reference to two SPEN connection offers; voltage, capacity, connection date and substation are all unknown.

aliases.alias: Southside Data Centre, Land at Clawbare Cottage, Longformacus

project.summary: Proposed 225 MW data centre campus ('Southside') on moorland and farmland of the Roxburghe Estate at Clawbare Cottage, between Longformacus and Westruther in the Lammermuir Hills, about 11 km west of Duns. Promoted by Sunlaws Development Company Limited (SC121007), a Roxburghe Estates entity. Three two-storey buildings up to 24 m high with an 8.1 ha ground footprint are proposed, marketed as using curtailed local wind generation via the Fallago Rig substation, with a claimed £2bn investment and construction from about 2029 for 2030 operation. EIA screening (25/01835/SCR) concluded in February 2026 that EIA is required; a PAN and June 2026 consultations followed. EIA scoping case 26/01031/SCO was received and validated on 8 July 2026, and Scottish Borders Council issued its scoping opinion on 31 August 2026. No full planning application has been lodged (expected no earlier than late 2026). A 'Save the Lammermuirs' campaign opposes the scheme.
project.maturity_explanation: Pre-application stage with formal early steps completed: EIA screening 25/01835/SCR concluded on 27 February 2026 that EIA is required; a Proposal of Application Notice was accepted and statutory consultation events were held on 4 and 10 June; EIA scoping case 26/01031/SCO was validated on 8 July and the council issued its scoping opinion on 31 August 2026. No planning application for permission has been validated, so the project remains M1, not M2.

latest_development.headline: Scottish Borders Council issues the EIA scoping opinion for 26/01031/SCO, following receipt and validation on 8 July 2026

unknowns: Exact planning reference and acceptance date for the PAN

Full text of the EIA screening opinion of 27 February 2026 and the council's scoping-response documents (the official case metadata was verified, but document downloads were unavailable during refresh)
Whether total floorspace is 54,000 m2 per building (Border Telegraph) or 54,000 m2 across the three buildings (trade-press phrasing is ambiguous)
Whether the 225 MW figure is IT load, grid import capacity, or total site demand, and whether any grid connection application/offer exists with SP Energy Networks / SP Transmission or NESO
Precise site boundary and the split between moorland and farmland; agricultural land classification not published
Formal positions of Duns and Longformacus & District community councils (none located)
Methodology and author of the preliminary economic study (£47m Borders value over 15 years; £776m tax over 15 years)
Relationship, if any, between the mains-gas backup generation described in the screening-stage reporting and the later 'no diesel backup generators' statement

site_area_m2.claimant: Trade press description of the 151 ha campus (echoed in project briefing material)
site_area_m2.notes: 151 ha figure appears in trade-press summaries of the EIA material; not verified against a red-line plan because the SBC portal was unreachable. The built ground footprint is much smaller (see building_footprint_m2).

building_footprint_m2.claimant: Sunlaws Development Company Limited (EIA screening description)
building_footprint_m2.notes: 8.1 ha total ground footprint for three two-storey data centre buildings; campaigners describe this as 'equivalent to 11 football pitches'.

gross_floor_area_m2.claimant: Border Telegraph reading of the screening submission (54,000 m2 internal floorspace per building x 3)
gross_floor_area_m2.notes: Border Telegraph states 54,000 m2 internal floorspace per building (50% IT halls, 50% mechanical/electrical); trade-press phrasing ('each spanning a total of 54,000 sqm') is ambiguous and could mean 54,000 m2 across all three. Unresolved conflict — 162,000 m2 recorded as the per-building reading, low confidence.

max_building_height_m.claimant: Sunlaws Development Company Limited (EIA screening description)

site.current_land_use: Upland moorland and farmland on the Roxburghe Estate in the Lammermuir Hills (APRS describes 'farmland and moorland'; developer proposes green roofs planted with moorland species)
site.land_notes: Site lies between Longformacus and Westruther in the Lammermuir Hills, reported as sitting between Dirrington Great Law and Dirrington Little Law with the Southern Upland Way passing nearby. Agricultural land classification and any formal landscape designations (e.g. whether within the Lammermuir Hills Special Landscape Area) could not be verified from available sources — no statutory designation was confirmed, so protected_designations is left empty rather than guessed. Coordinates are an approximate mid-point between Longformacus and Westruther near the Dirrington laws, not a surveyed centroid; no red-line boundary published, so no boundary polygon is provided.

capacity_claims.claimant: Sunlaws Development Company Limited (developer website and press briefing)
capacity_claims.preferred_rationale: Figure used consistently on the developer's own website and in trade-press summaries of the EIA material; the 220 MW figure appears only on the APRS campaign page and is likely a rounding or transcription variant.
capacity_claims.notes: Reported as the capacity the campus 'would offer' / 'consume approximately' at full build-out; whether this is IT load or grid import is not disclosed. Trade press also describes it as approximate electricity consumption at full capacity.

capacity_claims.claimant: Action to Protect Rural Scotland (campaign tracker page)
capacity_claims.notes: APRS describes 'a 220MW data centre on farmland and moorland on Roxburghe Estate'; conflicts with the developer's 225 MW figure and no provenance is given.

Screening-stage description (Dec 2025) refers to a mains gas connection with emergency backup gas generation for outages and testing; by June 2026 consultation reporting the developer stated no diesel backup generators are proposed. No capacity figure for backup generation disclosed, and the gas-backup position may have evolved.

energy_estimates.onsite_generation: None proposed for primary supply; screening-stage description included emergency backup gas generation via a mains gas connection, while June 2026 reporting states no diesel backup generators are proposed
energy_estimates.demand_flexibility: Developer markets the project as absorbing frequently curtailed local wind generation, but no flexibility mechanism, private wire or PPA has been evidenced
energy_estimates.notes: 'Powered entirely by renewable energy' / 'principally powered through local renewable energy' are developer claims with no stated matching method; 225 MW is the developer's full-capacity consumption figure, recorded here as peak load for want of a stated basis. No annual energy figure published.

water_estimates.cooling_description: Developer website states a 'closed loop cooling system, not connected to interrupt local water supplies', and consultation publicity says the upland site 'lends itself to keeping the centre at optimum low temperatures without the need for water cooling'. However, the earlier screening-stage description referred to water supply from Scottish Water and a borehole requiring a SEPA licence — the purpose (cooling vs domestic/initial fill) is not stated.
water_estimates.notes: No quantified water figures published at this pre-application stage; the closed-loop/no-water-cooling claim and the Scottish Water + borehole supply described at screening stage should be reconciled against the EIA when submitted.

economic_claims.notes: Described variously as '£2 billion investment in the Scottish economy when the building is operational'; unclear whether this is construction capex, cumulative economic contribution, or asset value. No methodology published.
The headline '145 high-quality local jobs' is broken down by the developer as 100 direct and 45 indirect. FTE vs headcount unstated; no methodology published.
Indirect component of the 145 local jobs claim.
'More than 250 jobs elsewhere in Scotland' — direct/indirect/induced split and methodology unstated; treated as a minimum ('over 250').

'Around 1,000 jobs during the construction phase' — unclear whether peak workforce, total headcount or job-years; recorded as peak_construction_workforce as the most common reading, but the category is not stated by the claimant.
'£25 million annually to the Scottish economy' — whether GVA or gross output unstated.
'Around £12 million each year for the Borders' — subset of the £25m Scotland figure; measure (GVA vs output) unstated.

economic_claims.claimant: Sunlaws Development Company Limited (citing a preliminary economic study)
economic_claims.methodology: Described only as a 'preliminary economic study'; author, model and assumptions not published
economic_claims.notes: '£47 million additional value to the Scottish Borders over the first 15 years' — recorded as GVA on the 'additional value' wording, but the measure is not explicitly defined.

economic_claims.claimant: Sunlaws Development Company Limited (as reported by Border Telegraph)
economic_claims.notes: '£776 million tax revenue over 15 years' — reported once; the tax base (non-domestic rates vs all taxes) is unstated, so the business_rates category is an approximation. Sits awkwardly against the £25m/yr economic-contribution figure and needs verification against the source study.

community.summary: Organised local opposition emerged quickly after the PAN through Save the Lammermuirs. Its online petition was reported at more than 6,000 signatures by mid-June 2026, APRS's coalition letter recorded 25,085 as at 22 August, and the live petition displayed 41,907 when checked on 3 September. The page also showed a sharp same-day increase, so the stability and geographic origin of that total have not been verified. Around 170 residents attended the two statutory consultation events in June, at which the Duke of Roxburghe and Roxburghe Estates MD Jaap Röell appeared for the developer. Concerns centre on landscape and visual impact in the Lammermuir Hills, energy demand, noise, traffic and dark skies. No formal positions from Duns or Longformacus & District community councils were located.

project.summary: A '200 MW data centre proposed for the Gogar area of Edinburgh' that was 'deemed not to need an EIA' is cited by SPICe (June 2026) without developer, reference or further detail. Systematic searches of the City of Edinburgh Council planning record (via the PlanIt mirror of citydev-portal) found no data centre application at Gogar or Gogarburn. The reference is almost certainly a conflation with one of two verified Edinburgh schemes tracked separately: the Shelborn Drummond 212.42 MW 'Green Data Centre' at 1 Redheughs Avenue, South Gyle (EIA screened out under 25/03575/SCR; called 'the Gogarburn data centre' by APRS because the former RBS Drummond House site sits by the NatWest Gogarburn campus), or the Apatura Wester Hermiston 200 MW campus at Riccarton (EIA screened out under 25/02924/SCR and again under 25/05576/SCR), whose 200 MW figure exactly matches SPICe's. project.canonical_name: Killellan AI Growth Zone (Killellan Farm, Toward)
project.summary: Marketed hyperscale AI campus at Killellan Farm, Toward, on the Cowal peninsula south of Dunoon (not Kintyre — the similarly named Killean in Kintyre is a different place). Argyll Data Development Ltd and Argyll Energy Development Ltd (two small companies registered at the farm, directors Peter Griffiths and landowner Robert Mitchell) bid in May 2025 for UK Government AI Growth Zone designation of a 184-acre quarry-and-farmland site, and in October 2025 announced a strategic partnership with SambaNova Systems claiming a 100-600 MW first phase, 2 GW+ full build-out and £15bn investment. The only planning consent that exists is a 2020 delegated permission (20/00229/PP) for a single data-storage building of modest scale, kept alive by a March 2025 certificate of lawful commencement; no application, PAN, screening or scoping for the main campus has been located on the Argyll and Bute portal. The sovereign AI cloud 'launched' in May 2026 runs from other, undisclosed UK data centres. The gap between headline claims (up to 10 GW connectivity, £15bn) and consented reality (one small building; a developer-stated 6 MW grid application) is the largest in this dataset.
project.maturity_explanation: The marketed 100-600 MW / 2 GW+ campus is concept-stage: no planning application, PAN, EIA screening or scoping for it exists on the Argyll and Bute portal as of 30 Jul 2026. The only consent is 20/00229/PP (approved 15 May 2020) for one Class 4 data-storage building, with lawful commencement certified via 25/00445/CLAWU (28 Mar 2025). That small consented element alone might merit M3, but it is not the announced project; the campus itself is M0 with M1 features (land control, AI Growth Zone bid, initial £15m raise).

site.land_notes: Coordinates are an approximate placement of Killellan Farm/quarry area between Toward and Ardyne, from OSM features; no red-line boundary has been published, so no boundary.geojson is provided. Site access stated as via the Killellan Farm entrance from the A815. Developer describes the site as 'industrially zoned'; APRS describes it as brownfield and farmland. Note the place-name: council and developer records use 'Killellan' (Toward, Cowal); 'Killean' is a different settlement in Kintyre — APRS's use of 'Killean' is a variant/erroneous spelling. Official red-line area (Spatial Hub, planning application boundary): 0.4 ha; previously recorded 74.5 ha (developer-stated campus); difference -99.4%. CORROBORATION, not a discrepancy: the only official red line at Killellan encloses ~0.4 ha - the single small data-storage building consented in 2020 (20/00229/PP). The 74.5 ha figure is the promoted campus, which has no application. The official geometry is direct documentary support for the finding that the multi-gigawatt claim rests on one small consent.

Main campus (100-600 MW / 2 GW+ on ~74 ha): NO planning application, proposal of application notice (PAN), EIA screening or scoping request located on the Argyll and Bute Public Access portal as of 30 July 2026. project.summary: Proposed 300 MW AI data centre campus by Apatura (applicant Apatura DC Project 5 Ltd) on ~55 acres of Scottish Enterprise-owned land at Glenbervie Business Park, Bellsdyke Road/Stirling Road, Larbert, Falkirk. community.summary: The application attracted one of the largest public responses recorded on Falkirk Council's portal: about 6,700 objections against 80 messages of support by the 2 July 2026 consultation close, rising to more than 7,100 comments in late-July reporting. An APRS coalition letter published on 23 August recorded 7,020 objections uploaded to the portal as at 22 August; the figures may reflect different cut-offs or categories. Organised opposition includes Say No To Larbert Data Centre, The Inches and Kinnaird Village Residents Association and Larbert Residents Association, alongside APRS and Stop Climate Chaos Scotland. A Change.org petition was recorded at 5,402 signatures on 22 August and displayed 5,884 when checked on 3 September. More than 100 people attended a protest on 13 August, while APRS described the attendance as hundreds. Police Scotland's consultation response anticipated substantial public opposition and recommended robust site security. Apatura and Scottish Enterprise present the scheme as major inward investment with jobs and green-design commitments.

principal_concerns.concern: Proximity to sensitive uses — objectors state the site is close to housing, a nursery and Forth Valley Royal Hospital, and reportedly only ~20 m from a care home
Air quality and noise from 200 emergency backup diesel generators (campaigners compare emissions to '106,000 idling diesel cars' during testing)
principal_concerns.developer_response: Apatura states generators are for emergency backup only with periodic testing, and that the campus is designed to green-charter standards.

principal_concerns.concern: Scale of electricity demand (300MW; combined with Auchtertool, Fife, 900MW — just under a quarter of Scottish peak demand) and possible impact on energy prices

Adequacy of consultation and of environmental information; complexity of a 52-document environmental submission; APRS argues the proposal is contrary to the development plan and calls for a moratorium on hyperscale AI data centres
Water use and pressure concerns (drawing on reported experience near US data centres)
principal_concerns.developer_response: Apatura states a closed-loop cooling system will minimise water use.

'District heat ready' design offering potential future heat supply to local homes/businesses; no off-taker, network or funding identified
Almost £1bn of direct investment in Scotland

project.summary: SIMEC Atlantis Energy (now SAE Renewables) announced in 2019 a 'world's first ocean-powered' hyperscale data centre in Caithness, supplied by private wire from an expanded MeyGen tidal array, targeting operation by 2024. An EIA screening request for a data centre at Mey (20/01258/SCRE) was decided by Highland Council in March 2020, but no application followed and the original timeline lapsed. The 20+ ha SAE-owned greenfield site is now marketed by Invest Highland as an investment opportunity; SAE's current planning activity at Mey is a 300 MW battery storage scheme.

No planning application, PAN or scoping has followed in six years; the site is now marketed as an opportunity, so M1 reflects the highest evidenced stage of a currently dormant proposal.

project.summary: Proposed AI-focused hyperscale data centre campus promoted by ILI Group on Green Belt farmland at North Lanrigg, between Newhouse, Cleland, Chapelhall and Holytown in North Lanarkshire, badged at 400MW. The third of ILI's three 'Stoics' sites (with Cato in Fife and Rufus in East Ayrshire) in a claimed £15bn programme. A Proposal of Application Notice (25/00989/PAN) was lodged with North Lanarkshire Council in September 2025, pre-application exhibitions were held in October-November 2025, and an EIA screening opinion request (26/00595/EIASCR, 'Data Centre Campus Including Grid Connection') was lodged in May 2026 and remained undetermined as of late July 2026. project.summary: Proposed c. 212.4 MW hyperscale 'green' data centre by Shelborn Drummond Ltd (Shelborn Asset Management group) on the 5.74 ha former RBS headquarters site at 1 Redheughs Avenue, South Gyle/Edinburgh Park, Edinburgh. Planning permission in principle (25/04239/PPP) for a two-building campus was refused unanimously by City of Edinburgh Council in February 2026. Shelborn appealed (DPEA PPA-230-2794). A 30 July screening direction required an Environmental Impact Assessment and the appellant confirmed on 12 August that it would submit an EIA Report. Scottish Ministers recalled the appeal on 17 August; the DPEA case is now on hold for ministerial consideration, with a revised target date of 28 September 2026. This is the highest-profile Scottish data centre refusal case to date.

Scottish Ministers recalled the appeal on 17 August 2026 and it remains live but on hold for ministerial consideration, rather than being a lapsed scheme.

planning_cases.decision_notes: Refused unanimously by the Development Management Sub-Committee on 4 February 2026 against the officer recommendation of approval, after a hearing (data centre debated for nearly two hours of a four-hour meeting); formal decision date 9 February 2026 per the DPEA record. Refusal grounds as summarised by APRS: contrary to NPF4 Policy 1 (climate and nature crises), contrary to NPF4 Policy 2 (failure to address lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions), and contrary to City Plan 2030 Place 19 (does not support the mixed-use vision for the Edinburgh Park/South Gyle area). Committee debate focused on the undefined status of a 'green data centre' under NPF4, unevidenced renewable power supply figures, cooling and water uncertainty, deliverability of waste heat re-use, limited job creation (council consultation-response estimate of 39 jobs against over 200 proposed parking spaces), and impacts (noise, visual, security fencing, generator flues, diesel generator use) on the consented mixed-use development including housing c. 50 m away.

community.summary: The application attracted sustained opposition from October 2025, led by APRS with a local residents' campaign group (WhatsApp/Instagram based), and protests outside the City Chambers before the 4 February 2026 committee hearing. Concerns centred on climate impact and 'greenwashing' of the green data centre label, the decision not to require an EIA, diesel backup generators near planned housing and a nursery, energy/grid demand, and minimal job creation against the mixed-use vision for Edinburgh Park. Councillors from all parties echoed these concerns and refused unanimously against officer advice. At appeal, 38 representations were lodged with the DPEA, including from APRS and ERCS Legal. The appellant confirmed on 12 August 2026 that it would submit an EIA Report, and Scottish Ministers recalled the appeal on 17 August for their own consideration.

project.summary: Proposed 200 MW 'AI data centre campus' by Apatura (SPV Apatura DC Project 11 Ltd) on Green Belt farmland at Wester Hermiston, north of Heriot-Watt University's Riccarton campus and west of the Edinburgh City Bypass, near Currie. A Proposal of Application Notice (25/03978/PAN) was submitted on 1 August 2025 for a forthcoming full ('national development') planning application. City of Edinburgh Council concluded twice that EIA was not required (25/02924/SCR on 7 July 2025 and 25/05576/SCR on 6 May 2026), but a third-party screening-direction request was received by Scottish Government Planning and Architecture on 18 May 2026. Scottish Ministers issued their direction on 17 August 2026: an EIA is required. Design documents describe three data centre buildings totalling c.54,690 m2 footprint connected to Currie Substation, with £1.4bn claimed investment. A local campaign, APRS and the Cockburn Association oppose or question the scheme, in the wake of the refusal of the nearby South Gyle data centre in February 2026.
project.maturity_explanation: PAN submitted 1 August 2025 and reported to the Development Management Sub-Committee on 25 March 2026 as a 'forthcoming application'. Two council EIA screenings concluded EIA was not required, but Scottish Ministers' later direction EIA-230-002, issued 17 August 2026, requires an Environmental Impact Assessment. Early development remains M1, not M2: no validated full planning application for the data centre itself has been verified.

community.summary: Significant organised local and city-wide opposition at pre-application stage. A local residents' campaign (Hermiston Data Centre Campaign) and a Change.org petition (3,581 signatures by July 2026) oppose the scheme; APRS campaigns against it nationally; the Cockburn Association questions 'green' claims without opposing data centres outright. The February 2026 refusal of the nearby South Gyle data centre and the council Planning Committee's June 2026 call for a Scottish Government moratorium on large-scale data centres form the political backdrop. Following a third-party request, Scottish Ministers directed on 17 August 2026 that an Environmental Impact Assessment is required. The PAN was notified to Currie and Ratho Community Councils, Pentland Hills ward councillors, Gordon MacDonald MSP and Dr Scott Arthur MP; formal representations will only be counted once an application is submitted.

project.summary: Apatura proposes a 300MW AI data centre campus with a co-located 500MW battery energy storage system on land adjacent to Crosshill Road, Westerhill, north-east of Bishopbriggs, within East Dunbartonshire Council's adopted Westerhill Regeneration Area masterplan. The data centre would be consented by the council; the BESS is intended to be consented separately under section 36 via the Energy Consents Unit. As of July 2026 the project is at pre-application stage: an EIA screening opinion (TP/ED/25/0245) concluded EIA is required, and a Proposal of Application Notice (TP/ED/25/0428) was lodged in August 2025, but no full planning application or s36 application has been located.

src-stv-community.title: Fife community 'taken aback' at scale of plans for data centre
src-stv-community.notes: Auchtertool ~215 houses; three-year build programme cited; ACC chair Andrea Cail quotes on water/discharge/electricity uncertainty; ILI cites cooler climate for 'free cooling' and proximity to wind farms and battery storage; site plans 'up to seven buildings and an on-site substation' (per related search excerpt).

src-acc-village-update.title: Update on Proposed Datacentre Near Auchtertool (community council update, Nov 2025)
src-acc-village-update.perspective: Community council acting as neutral facilitator at that stage
src-acc-village-update.notes: Pre-application stage (Nov 2025): access from B925 west of Auchtertool; ~25% of site visible from most of the village; buildings 30-35 m; developer then indicated 30-50 permanent jobs and up to 1,000 construction jobs; possible district heating; water mains pipe too small, new pipe likely required; Scottish Water Horizons involved; application then targeted for Q1 2026.

src-abdnshire-portal-app-2016-0766.title: Planning application APP/2016/0766 — Mixed Use Development Comprising Town Centre ... Land to West and South West of Rifle Range, Blackdog, Aberdeen
src-abdnshire-portal-app-2016-0766.notes: The portal (upa.aberdeenshire.gov.uk) was unreachable during this research session (HTTP 503 / connection reset, apparent WAF blocking). Reference, description and site address corroborated via the Scottish Government notification record (src-govscot-na-abs-045) and APRS page. src-govscot-na-abs-045.title: Planning decision NA-ABS-045: mixed use development on land at Blackdog, Aberdeen (F/APP/2016/0766)
src-govscot-na-abs-045.notes: Notified application; case closed 2017-08-22, 'cleared back to the planning authority for their own determination'. Confirms proposal description: mixed use town centre incl. regional food hall, retail, leisure, Class 3, business/industrial (Classes 4,5,6), A90 access alterations, low carbon infrastructure, at land to west and south west of rifle range, Blackdog.

src-ashfield-2016-application.title: Major new planning application set to transform Blackdog, Aberdeenshire
src-ashfield-2016-application.notes: £150m mixed-use application lodged 2016 with Kirkwood Homes: 600 houses (150 affordable), regional food hall, hotel, cinema, retail, offices/industrial, park & ride, primary school site. Claims for that scheme: 1,200 construction jobs, 1,500 FT jobs long term, £586m salaries over 25 years, £1.56bn GVA. Site allocated in 2012 Aberdeenshire LDP; Blackdog Masterplan approved 2013; on Energetica corridor at A90/AWPR junction.

src-ashfield-2017-consent.title: Blackdog, Aberdeen granted planning permission
src-ashfield-2017-consent.notes: Reports unanimous approval of the £150m town-centre/mixed-use plans by Aberdeenshire councillors on 2017-04-27; Kirkwood Homes housing on same site approved the month before (March 2017). Note tension with src-govscot-na-abs-045: application was notified to Scottish Ministers and only cleared back on 2017-08-22, so the formal decision notice post-dates the committee approval.

src-energetica-blackdog.title: Blackdog Project — Energetica corridor key projects page
src-energetica-blackdog.publisher: Energetica (Aberdeen City & Shire / Opportunity North East partnership)
src-energetica-blackdog.notes: Describes 71-acre mixed-use development; first phase (48 houses) granted permission November 2015; applications March 2016; unanimous Formartine Committee approval March 2017 and full council approval April 2017; repeats 1,200 construction / 1,500 net additional FT jobs, £586m salaries, £1.56bn GVA claims for the mixed-use scheme.

src-aprs-blackdog.title: Blackdog, north of Aberdeen — APRS data centre campaign page (includes developer press release text, 22 April 2026)
src-aprs-blackdog.perspective: Campaign group critical of hyperscale data centres in Scotland
src-aprs-blackdog.notes: Identifies the prior consent relied on by the developers as PPiP APP/2016/0766 and quotes them saying they 'believe plans for the multi-billion pound data centre would align with these conditions'; states detailed planning yet to be submitted. Reproduces the full 22 April 2026 developer press release (600MW initial, multi-GW ambition, 1,000 construction / 100 permanent / 2,000 indirect jobs, >£10bn per GW, Cerulean Winds Aspen private-wire discussions, True North Advisors/Diffley Partnership poll 62% of 1,303 in favour, ONE and ETZ Ltd support). Also flags toxic oil & gas waste dump in dunes directly south of the site.

src-digit-600mw.title: Aberdeen tipped for 600MW AI campus, powered by offshore wind
src-digit-600mw.notes: 600MW first phase, consent 'secured for first phase', ground-breaking hoped 2026 subject to commercial agreements; up to 1,000 construction jobs, 100 permanent high-skilled, 2,000 indirect; Cerulean Winds Aspen discussions; >£10bn per GW.

src-abn-blackdog.title: Blackdog poised for multi-billion-pound data centre
src-abn-blackdog.notes: 200 acres incl. former MoD firing range; initial 600MW renewable and grid-connected power; claimed access to 3GW of renewable wind energy; ScotWind/INTOG and subsea-cable claims; jobs figures as press release; no application reference given.

src-pj-datacentre.title: Multi-billion-pound data centre plan for Blackdog near Aberdeen
src-pj-datacentre.notes: Cited via search results only (page not retrievable in this environment). APRS identifies the P&J as the outlet that carried the developer press release.

src-dcd-blackdog.title: 600MW data center could be built near Aberdeen, Scotland — report
src-dcd-blackdog.notes: Page returned 403; content known via search excerpts: 200-acre site 5 miles north of Aberdeen; Ashfield Land + TechRE; 600MW initial scaling to multi-gigawatts; consent secured for first phase; possible private-wire and international subsea cables.

src-pj-landfill.title: Oil waste to finally be removed from former notorious north-east landfill (Blackdog)
src-pj-landfill.notes: Via search excerpts: Blackdog landfill took ~70% of offshore waste landed in the north-east in the 1980s; used from ~1930s to 1980s; Aberdeenshire Council designated site, beach and dunes contaminated land in 2004; FCC Environment UK remediation project approved 2019. The dump lies in the dunes directly south of the development site (per APRS).

src-ch-ashfield-aberdeen.notes: Active; incorporated 2015-06-11; registered office St Catherine's Court, Berkeley Place, Clifton, Bristol BS8 1BQ (Ashfield Land group address); SIC 68100 buying and selling of own real estate; accounts to 2025-03-31 filed.

src-ch-blackdog-land.notes: Incorporated 2013-09-03, registered at 7 Golden Square, Aberdeen AB10 1EP. PSCs: Alexander Barclay Thow and Jacqueline Thow (each 25-50% shares/votes). Relationship to the data centre consortium not established — recorded as a possibly related land entity only.

src-urbanrealm-2017.title: £150m Aberdeenshire leisure destination secures green light

src-bbc-rufus-2026.title: Could a huge data centre revitalise Ayrshire – or ruin it? (BBC Glasgow and West, Jonathan Geddes, 1 March 2026; accessed via repost)

src-ili-rufus-consultation.title: Rufus Data Centre Project — pre-application consultation page
src-ili-rufus-consultation.notes: Describes an AI-focused data centre near Hurlford 'entirely powered by off-site renewable energy sources'; lists consultation events 24 Feb 2026 (Park Hotel, Kilmarnock), 3 Mar 2026 (Hurlford Community Centre), 11 Mar 2026 (Galston Community Centre); claims 'hundreds of jobs during construction and skilled tech jobs when operating'; community support offers (school transport, defibrillators, local funding).

src-ili-data-centres.title: Data Centres — The Stoics
src-ili-data-centres.notes: Claims each Stoics site 'has secured grid connection, land rights, and has entered the planning process'; 'tens of billions of pounds in private investment'; 'thousands of construction jobs at peak'; renewable power / net-zero and heat-recovery claims. No site-specific figures for Rufus.

src-bdc-stoics-2025.title: ILI Group Launches The Stoics – A £15 Billion Green Data Centre Network
src-bdc-stoics-2025.notes: Trade press coverage of the 4 Nov 2025 Stoics launch: £15bn total investment across Cato (Fife), Rufus (East Ayrshire), Aurelius (North Lanarkshire); Mark Wilson (CEO) quote.

src-yahoo-glasgowlive-rufus-2025.title: Massive data centre plan for Ayrshire is part of £15 billion investment (syndicated)
src-yahoo-glasgowlive-rufus-2025.notes: Reports 540MW capacity for Rufus; site at Purroch Farm just north of HMP Kilmarnock; first Stoics phase targeted online by 2027; Logan Energy Project Management involvement; describes application as awaiting determination on East Ayrshire's portal (the record concerned is the pre-application 25/0008/PREAPP).

src-aprs-hurlford.title: ILI Rufus by Hurlford
src-aprs-hurlford.perspective: Countryside-protection campaign body running a national data centres campaign; opposed to greenfield data centre development
src-aprs-hurlford.notes: Describes a 540MW data centre on farmland on the edge of Hurlford, 'currently in the pre-application stage'; links portal reference 25/0008/PREAPP, the developer consultation page, a local campaign Facebook group (facebook.com/groups/1604173331036496) and campaign website (ayrshiremajordev.wixsite.com/hurlforddevelopment).

src-amdcg-proposal.title: The Proposal — Hurlford Development
src-amdcg-proposal.perspective: Volunteer-run local community campaign group critical of the proposal
src-amdcg-proposal.notes: States 540MW base power capacity 'before any future expansion'; pre-application submitted November 2025; concerns: scale, absence of EIA to date, water use for cooling, electricity demand, wildlife, landscape, and residents' exclusion from early engagement.

src-ch-ili-rufus.title: ILI RUFUS LIMITED (SC825440) — Companies House record
