References 25/00838/PAN and 25/00556/EIA and the screening outcome are corroborated only via secondary sources (APRS, datacentermap, Bylines). An Idox keyVal T0BHY2BA0EC00 is reported by Bylines for one of the records. Needs direct verification.

src-apatura-news-ravenscraig.title: Ravenscraig — plans to transform former steelworks into one of the UK's largest green AI data centres
src-apatura-news-ravenscraig.notes: Launch announcement: 550 MW of grid connections operational by 2030; £3.9bn estimated construction cost; 'independent socio-economic study' (consultant unnamed) claiming £1.2bn one-off construction GVA, 16,000+ job years, £729m annual GVA, 2,399 long-term jobs (direct, indirect and induced), +0.4% Scottish GDP; AI Growth Zone bid submitted to DSIT; Apatura states it controls 1.6GW+ of grid connections across five central-belt sites. Same text carried on ravenscraig.co.uk.

src-apatura-consult-ravenscraig-project.title: Ravenscraig AI Energy Campus — consultation project page and timeline
src-apatura-consult-ravenscraig-project.notes: 550 MW data centre; 650 MW BESS (to be consented via separate Section 36 application to the Energy Consents Unit); sites east and west of the Ravenscraig masterplan area — eastern plot six data halls, western plot three buildings; direct connection to high-capacity substations at Wishaw and Newarthill; grid offer accepted June 2025 via NESO. Timeline: consultations Q3 2025, planning application Q4 2025, decision Q1 2026, construction 2026-2028, operations 2029.

src-apatura-consult-ravenscraig-event.title: Ravenscraig AI Energy Campus — public consultation event page
src-apatura-consult-ravenscraig-event.notes: Public consultation event Monday 6 October 2025, 3pm-8pm, Wellbeing Academy, New College Lanarkshire, 1 Enterprise Way, Motherwell ML1 2TX.

src-publicnoticeportal-pan.title: Public notice — Apatura DC Project 2 Ltd, notice of intention to submit a planning application, Land at Ravenscraig Regeneration Area, Wishaw, Motherwell ML1 1NR
src-publicnoticeportal-pan.notes: Statutory pre-application notice: 'Erection of an AI Data Centre Campus with a 550MW demand utility capacity with ancillary Battery Energy Storage (to be consented via separate Section 36 application to the ECU), car parking, landscaping, roads, access and associated works'. Applicant named as Apatura DC Project 2 Ltd. Direct fetch returned HTTP 404 during the session; text recovered via search index, so marked broken pending re-check.

src-hlws1290.title: Lanarkshire AI Growth Zone Designation and Delivery Update (written statement HLWS1290)
src-hlws1290.notes: Lanarkshire named fifth AI Growth Zone, delivered by DataVita in partnership with CoreWeave: 3,400+ jobs, £8.2bn private investment, £540m community commitment over 15 years, up to 500 MW of compute on a site drawing on on-site renewables (heat reuse explored for University Hospital Monklands). Ravenscraig/Apatura is not named. Page returned 403 to direct fetch; content assembled from search index and secondary reporting.

src-nlc-news-aigz.title: Plans welcomed for North Lanarkshire to become one of the world's most advanced AI sites
src-nlc-news-aigz.notes: Council welcome of the AI Growth Zone designation: DataVita (Chapelhall-based) with CoreWeave; £8.2bn investment, up to 3,400 direct and up to 7,000 wider regional jobs, £543m community fund. Does not mention the Ravenscraig data campus. Notes all proposals remain subject to statutory planning approval.

src-datavita-aigz-faq.title: Lanarkshire AI Growth Zone — FAQs
src-datavita-aigz-faq.notes: AIGZ comprises 500 MW of data centre capacity, 1GW+ private-wire renewables (800 MW wind, 400 MW+ solar) and an AI Innovation Park; community fund up to £543m over 15 years (£50k/MW data centre + £15k/MW renewables annually). Ravenscraig and Apatura are not mentioned.

src-ch-ravenscraig-ltd.notes: Active private limited company, incorporated 23 December 1998 (formerly Stamek Limited to Feb 2000), registered office c/o Brodies LLP, Edinburgh. Three active PSCs, each holding 25-50% of shares and voting rights: Scottish Enterprise; Wilson Bowden (Ravenscraig) Limited (04199662, part of Barratt); Tata Steel UK Limited.

src-dcd-apatura-ravenscraig.title: Apatura plans 500MW data center campus in Scotland
src-dcd-apatura-ravenscraig.notes: Reports the £3.9bn / 550 MW proposal on the ~160-acre 'SevenFourEight' site east of the Wishaw Deviation freight railway line, online target 2030; headline uses 500MW. Site 403'd to direct fetch; content via search index.

src-scn-consultation.title: Consultation continues for Ravenscraig AI energy campus
src-scn-consultation.notes: Second consultation event 6 October 2025; developer-reported 75% attendee support at first event; revised claims of over 2,000 jobs, £766m construction GVA and £583m annual GVA thereafter; submission to NLC intended before end-2025; completion 2029.

src-bylines-hyperscale.title: Best of Bylines: Hyperscale data centres — interrogating the 'green promise'
src-bylines-hyperscale.perspective: Critical of hyperscale data centre development
src-bylines-hyperscale.notes: States PAN submitted 2025 with 'no major impediments' identified; planning application expected summer 2026; cites 550 MW, a 600 MW battery storage facility (vs 650 MW in developer material), 160 acres, £3.9bn, and 'only 1,044 permanent jobs proposed'; notes Ravenscraig plus DataVita Airdrie exceed 1,000 MW proposed in North Lanarkshire; Idox keyVal T0BHY2BA0EC00.

src-datacentrenews-larbert.title: Apatura submits plans for Larbert data centre campus
src-datacentrenews-larbert.notes: Confirms that as of 11 June 2026 the Ravenscraig planning application had not yet been filed and was expected 'this summer'. Describes Apatura as Edinburgh/York-based with nine central-belt data centre locations, 1.6GW+ confirmed grid connections and 2.4GW Gate 2-compliant connections in total.

src-aprs-ravenscraig.title: Apatura Ravenscraig — campaign briefing page
src-aprs-ravenscraig.perspective: Campaign group opposed to unchecked data centre expansion
src-aprs-ravenscraig.notes: Used as lead-generation only. src-ravenscraig-vision.title: Vision — Ravenscraig regeneration (site history and joint venture)
src-ravenscraig-vision.notes: Describes Ravenscraig Ltd as a joint venture of Scottish Enterprise, Wilson Bowden Developments and Tata Steel regenerating the former Ravenscraig steelworks (closed 1992), one of Europe's largest brownfield regeneration sites.

src-aprs-drumshangie.title: Apatura Drumshangie

src-aprs-drumshangie.notes: Lists both PAN references (26/00069/PAN and 24/01025/PAN), PAN dates, coordinates, EIA screening outcome (EIA not required), 500MW grid application, Stanrigg disaster sensitivity, LDP history, and site-for-sale particulars link.

src-dcd-apatura-ravenscraig-bebeez.perspective: Trade press. Original DCD URL (https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/apatura-plans-500mw-data-center-campus-in-scotland/) returned 403 from the research environment; text read via BeBeez republication.

Also describes Apatura: founded 2014 per its own application, privately owned, claimed 10.6GW grid-secured portfolio incl. 1.8GW targeting data centres, five AI-ready central-belt sites.

src-wikipedia-stanrigg.title: Stanrigg mining accident
src-wikipedia-stanrigg.perspective: Crowd-sourced encyclopaedia; consistent with Scottish Mining Website and Northern Mine Research Society accounts.
src-wikipedia-stanrigg.notes: 9 July 1918 inrush at Arbuckle Pit, Stanrigg Colliery: 19 miners killed including six teenage boys; 11 bodies never recovered and remain entombed at the site; cause was subsidence/inrush of the overlying peat moss. Memorial (standing stone plus 19 stones) erected c.100 m from the accident site; centenary commemoration 2018.

src-nlc-eplanning-portal.title: North Lanarkshire Council ePlanning portal (Idox Public Access)
src-nlc-eplanning-portal.notes: Portal unreachable from the research environment on 2026-07-30 (TLS connection reset / HTTP 503 via proxy). PAN records 24/01025/PAN and 26/00069/PAN could therefore NOT be verified against the primary record; details rest on APRS and the selling agent's particulars. Re-check needed.

src-nac-26-00138-eia.title: 26/00138/EIA — Request for EIA Scoping Opinion for new data centre, Hunterston Estate, West Kilbride (North Ayrshire Idox portal record)
src-nac-26-00138-eia.notes: Received 25 Feb 2026, validated 27 Feb 2026, consultation to 13 Mar 2026, decision 'Scoping Agreed' issued 30 Mar 2026 (delegated). Applicant listed as Tetra Tech F.A.O. Stuart Murison (consultant acting for developer). Case officer Iain Davies; ward North Coast; Fairlie Community Council area. 12 documents including EIA scoping report (doc id 1330826) and consultation responses from Transport Scotland, SEPA, flood, Scottish Water, environmental health, roads, HSE, West of Scotland Archaeology Service, Historic Environment Scotland and NatureScot.

src-eneus-hunterston-page.title: Hunterston Data Centre — project page
src-eneus-hunterston-page.notes: States: ~164-acre site; developed by Eneus Energy and Revera Energy on Hunterston Estate land; Carlyle and GIC backing Eneus; transmission-level grid connection; closed-loop cooling with minimal water in normal operation, initial fill trucked in, supply confirmed from Scottish Water Camphill WTW; batteries for ~10 minutes ride-through plus standby generators up to 48 hours; investment expected to exceed £10bn; 1,000+ construction jobs; operational job numbers 'under review'; application expected 2026, construction 2027/28.

src-aprs-hunterston.title: Hunterston Data Centre (case page)
src-aprs-hunterston.perspective: Campaign group opposing rural data centre development
src-aprs-hunterston.notes: States: EIA scoping report submitted Feb 2026; site 88.16 ha of Grade 3 agricultural land just north of West Kilbride next to Hunterston Power Station; building footprint up to 300,000 m2 across ~30 ha, buildings up to 35 m; APRS infers 'at least 500MW' hyperscale; states a 450MW BESS on/adjacent to the site got planning permission in 2022 and is under construction; construction 2027 for ~7 years to 2034. Page content retrieved via search excerpts; direct fetch returned empty (likely bot-blocking).

src-ayrshire-today-archaeology.title: Archaeological concerns over Hunterston data centre plan
src-ayrshire-today-archaeology.notes: Reports scoping opinion agreed; up to 6 buildings initially, 300,000 m2 combined footprint, up to 35 m high; 300-space car parking, substations, underground cabling, generators, cooling plant; construction 2027 for ~7 years to 2034. West of Scotland Archaeological Service: site of 'high archaeological potential'; trenchless cabling could destroy buried remains; historic landscape connections to Hunterston House and Castle need protection; recommends non-invasive survey plus trial trenching before determination.

src-ess-news-revera-bess.title: Revera takes final investment decision on 800 MWh BESS near former UK nuclear plants
src-ess-news-revera-bess.notes: Revera Energy (Carlyle-backed) FID June 2026 on 400 MW / 800 MWh Hunterston BESS ~1 mile from Hunterston A/B; construction expected Q3 2026; direct transmission connection (TEC register); 400 kV substation construction underway; part of 1 GW/2 GWh Scottish portfolio (>£500m); developer estimates ~550 direct construction jobs and 45 long-term operational jobs across portfolio.

src-irvine-times-greens.title: Scottish Greens call for pause to Ayrshire data centre plans

Edinburgh data centre records are all at Riccarton/Currie (Apatura, 25/02924/SCR decided 'EIA Not Required' 2025-07-04; 25/05576/SCR decided 'EIA Not Required' 2026-05-06) and 1 Redheughs Avenue (Shelborn). Mirrors citydev-portal.edinburgh.gov.uk, which blocks the research environment.

src-ch-apatura-entity-search.title: Companies House search results for 'Apatura'
src-ch-apatura-entity-search.notes: Shows the Apatura group structure: Apatura DC Ltd (16041291) plus numbered SPVs Apatura DC Project 1-12 Ltd (e.g. Project 11 = 16470100, used for Wester Hermiston). The specific SPV for the Freeport/West Calder project could not be matched to a site from the register alone.

src-websearch-apatura-freeport-context.title: Press coverage identifying Freeport West Calder as one of Apatura's priority Scottish data centre sites (DCD 'Apatura plans 500MW data center campus in Scotland'; FutureScot)
src-websearch-apatura-freeport-context.notes: DCD article body not retrievable (403 from research environment); search-result extracts confirm Apatura's priority sites include 'Freeport in West Lothian' alongside Glenbervie, Ravenscraig, Wester Hermiston and Westerhill, all combined with BESS, and a claimed pipeline of 10.6GW including 2.6GW of AI-ready data centre capacity.

src-aprs-data-centre-map.title: Data Centre Map (interactive map and pipeline table, including note on five gate 2 grid-connection-only sites)
src-aprs-data-centre-map.perspective: Campaign group critical of hyperscale data centre development in Scotland; page last modified 2026-07-29
src-aprs-data-centre-map.notes: Key passage: 'These sites have applied for gate 2 grid connections that we have not otherwise seen elsewhere: Clydebridge (360MW), just outside Glasgow, Edzel (800MW) to be connected to the new Brechin substation, Inchinan (180MW), Jawcraig, Falkirk (180MW), and Easterhouse (500MW). This is from the Existing Agreements Register.' APRS spellings 'Edzel'/'Inchinan' assumed to mean Edzell and Inchinnan. The page's project table does NOT attribute these five sites to any developer.

src-neso-existing-agreements-register.title: Connections registers (Existing Agreements Register)
src-neso-existing-agreements-register.notes: Cited by APRS as the origin of the five gate 2 connection entries. The individual register rows (connectee names, connection sites, MW, agreement dates) were NOT independently extracted in this research pass; the register is published as bulk spreadsheets and the specific entries remain to be verified.

src-planit-api.title: PlanIt UK planning applications API — keyword searches for Clydebridge, Easterhouse, Inchinnan, Jawcraig and Edzell data centre records (negative results)
src-planit-api.notes: Searches run 2026-07-30 over 2019-01-01 to 2026-07-30: 'Clydebridge' (all authorities: 0 results); Glasgow + 'data centre' (no Easterhouse-area hyperscale record); Renfrewshire + 'data centre' (6 records, none at Inchinnan — two May 2025 withdrawn EIA screening requests for data centre campuses were at Gleniffer Road, Paisley and Caplaw Road, Neilston); 'Jawcraig' (0); Falkirk + 'data centre'; Angus + 'data centre' and + 'Edzell' (0). Used here as evidence of ABSENCE of planning records for these five sites.

src-osm-nominatim-settlements.title: OpenStreetMap Nominatim geocoding of Clydebridge (Clydebridge Steelworks, Cambuslang/Rutherglen), Easterhouse, Inchinnan and Edzell
src-osm-nominatim-settlements.notes: Settlement-level coordinates only; no site boundary is known for any of the five sites. Clydebridge Steelworks feature: 55.8327, -4.1850.

src-govuk-lanarkshire-aigz-2026.title: More than 3,400 jobs and targeted support for local communities as Lanarkshire named latest AI Growth Zone
src-govuk-lanarkshire-aigz-2026.perspective: Government promotional press release; jobs and investment figures are zone-level claims without published methodology
src-govuk-lanarkshire-aigz-2026.notes: Designation conditional on meeting agreed criteria and milestones. £8.2bn private investment; CoreWeave £1.5bn commitment; 3,400+ jobs (~800 'high-value AI roles', remainder construction/infrastructure); 50 apprenticeships; £543m community fund over 15 years; £5m UK government investment; 500MW+ on-site power generation; excess heat to University Hospital Monklands.

src-parl-hlws1290.title: Written statement HLWS1290 — AI Growth Zone: Lanarkshire (29 January 2026)
src-parl-hlws1290.notes: Lords written statement announcing the Lanarkshire AI Growth Zone designation (DataVita + CoreWeave anchor). Reference supplied by project brief; statement page not directly opened during this research pass.

src-coreweave-uk-15bn-2025.title: CoreWeave Announces £1.5 Billion Commitment to Power UK AI Innovation and Growth Through Sustainable Computing
src-coreweave-uk-15bn-2025.perspective: Corporate announcement of an investment commitment, not a disclosed contract
src-coreweave-uk-15bn-2025.notes: September 2025 announcement (timed with US state visit to the UK): £1.5bn UK commitment including deployment of NVIDIA Grace Blackwell Ultra GPUs at DataVita's Lanarkshire campus, renewable-backed with closed-loop cooling.

src-datavita-dv1-page.title: DV1 Data Centre Lanarkshire — Scotland's Tier III co-location facility
src-datavita-dv1-page.notes: DV1 'Fortis': Uptime Institute Tier III certified (design and construction), 24MW across 8,000 sqm, opened 2016, expandable to 40MW, 100% renewable energy claim.

src-datacentermap-dv1.title: DataVita DV1 — Lanarkshire Data Center (40 MW listing)
src-datacentermap-dv1.notes: Industry directory listing for DV1/Fortis; sister listing for DV3 at York Road exists.

src-dcd-dv3-2025.title: DataVita files to expand data center campus in Glasgow, Scotland
src-dcd-dv3-2025.notes: Reports DV3 filing on land adjacent to the Fortis (DV1) campus; DV1 described as Tier III, 24MW across 8,000 sqm, opened 2016, expandable to 40MW. Full text behind bot-block; details corroborated via search snippets and BeBeez syndication.

src-npm-dv3-approval.title: DataVita receives approval from North Lanarkshire Council for DV3 data centre plans
src-npm-dv3-approval.notes: DV3 approved across a 4.4-acre (~1.8ha) site on York Road, Chapelhall, adjacent to the existing Fortis campus; expected to comprise a three-storey building.

src-scn-aigz-2026.title: DataVita's North Lanarkshire site named UK AI Growth Zone
src-scn-aigz-2026.notes: £8.2bn designation; DataVita in partnership with CoreWeave; 500MW hyperscale capacity for AI workloads; 1GW+ private-wire renewables; PUE 1.15 and closed-loop cooling claims.

src-stv-south-lanridge-pan.title: Data centre plans for land near farm as North Lanarkshire Council given notice of application
src-stv-south-lanridge-pan.notes: Reports the HFD Renewables NL PAN at South Lanridge Farm, Newhouse: data centre plus other buildings, substation and battery energy storage; notice sent to council, MPs/MSPs and community councils; consultation events intended in April and June.

src-aprs-chapelhall-aigz.title: Chapelhall — AI Growth Zone (site-by-site analysis)
src-aprs-chapelhall-aigz.perspective: Campaign group opposed to Green Belt data centre development; useful for planning references, site identifications and document copies, but interpretive claims are contested
src-aprs-chapelhall-aigz.notes: Identifies DV4 = Lancaster Avenue (25/01322/PAN, 26/00707/EIASCR, screening report describes 'c.100-124MW green data centre', closed-loop cooling, DV4 consultation events 12 May / 2 June / 4 June 2026, FoI: 'DV4 will be driven by Scottish Power connections timescales which we expect to be brought forward to 2027'); DV6 = South Lanridge (25/01328/PAN, HFD Renewables NL, assumed location of most of the 500MW, BESS ~2,400MWh likely via ECU s36); DV1 extension 25/00150/FUL granted 2025-12-04 (NPF4 Policy 8), veteran 'Muirhead Oaks' felled Feb 2026; DV3 = 25/01159/PPP 40MW/1.8ha; APRS FoI analysis claims >90% of the 3,400 zone jobs are construction/indirect/induced; renewables adequacy critique; notes second AIGZ site planned in South Lanarkshire per FoI.

src-hfd-nlep.title: North Lanarkshire Energy Park
src-hfd-nlep.notes: HFD Renewables' private-wire energy park proposition supporting the data centre programme (wind, solar, BESS).

src-futurescot-coreweave-datavita.title: US hyperscaler to work with Scotland's DataVita as part of £1.5 billion investment in AI infrastructure
src-futurescot-coreweave-datavita.notes: September 2025 CoreWeave-DataVita partnership announcement coverage; describes DV1 as Scotland's largest data centre.
